summary:
Your 12-week average sits at 29.3 km/week across 27 runs, and the recent 4-week dip to 113 km (-9% vs the prior block) is modest enough to read as consolidation rather than any meaningful withdrawal from load — particularly given the 44 km long effort on June 8th, which anchors that window with real durability work.

The June 27th run stands out as the quality marker of the past fortnight: 15.7 km at 4:49/km with HR 161 is a strong aerobic output, sitting notably closer to threshold territory than your typical moderate-effort days. Today's LT test result — 4:24/km at 178 bpm — is a clean data point and will become more informative as the 30-day baseline builds. For now it establishes a reference: your June 27th average pace was within roughly 25 seconds of that threshold, which confirms it was a genuinely hard aerobic effort, not a tempo misread.

Daily steps averaging 14,120 over the past four weeks — including 11,641 on rest days — reflects a background activity floor that matters for durability and doesn't show up in run kilometres. Combined with the bike commute, your actual movement load is meaningfully higher than the running data alone suggests.
